ToolHeader.title: Uzbek Loan Receipt (Tilxat)
ToolHeader.description: Fill in a loan receipt — the sum is written out in words automatically, in Latin and Cyrillic script, ready to print.

witnesses.hint: Witnesses are not required, but they strengthen the document if a dispute arises.
witnesses.name: Witness {number} full name

preview.title: Document
preview.note: The signature is always handwritten. The safest form is for the borrower to copy the whole text by hand — handwriting can be verified by an expert. Empty fields print as writing lines, so a blank form can be printed and filled in by hand.

legal.question: Is a tilxat legally binding?
legal.answer: Yes. Under Article 733 of the Civil Code of Uzbekistan, a borrower's receipt means the loan agreement counts as concluded in written form. Above ten times the base calculation amount, written form is mandatory — and a tilxat is exactly what satisfies it. In a dispute, courts accept a tilxat as written evidence (sources: lex.uz, Civil Code Articles 732–733; regional Ministry of Justice guidance).

elements.question: What must a tilxat contain?
elements.answer: The elements required in legal practice: both parties' full names, passport details and registration addresses; the sum in digits AND in words; the date the money was given and the return deadline; how it was given (cash or card transfer); and the borrower's handwritten signature. This tool lays out every element, and writes the sum in words itself — so it cannot be mistyped.

handwritten.question: Is a printed tilxat valid, or must it be handwritten?
handwritten.answer: Both are valid, but the signature must always be by hand. Where a dispute is likely, having the borrower copy the whole text by hand is safer — handwriting can be examined by an expert. You can print this tool's output and sign it, or use it as the model to copy by hand.

notary.question: Does it need to be notarised?
notary.answer: No. A tilxat is binding without a notary. You may notarise it if you wish — it strengthens the evidence further — but the law does not require it.

currency.question: Why is the sum only in so'm?
currency.answer: Settlements between individuals in Uzbekistan are made in the national currency — lending in foreign currency conflicts with currency legislation. That is why this tool accepts and writes sums in so'm only.

privacy.question: Where does my data go?
privacy.answer: Nowhere. The whole document is composed in your browser: nothing is uploaded, nothing is stored. Close the page and the data is gone.
